rationale: The buyer is tightly defined — Craft CMS agencies and freelancers billing clients for HubSpot integrations in GDPR markets — and they have clear budget authority and a compliance urgency that justifies paying for a plugin ($99-199/site). The build is feasible: a Craft CMS/Formie plugin bridging HubSpot's Communication Preferences API is within Claude-assisted coding range, and delivery (plugin download + license key) is fully automatable. The total exactly meets min_total_to_build (6.5) but responsiveness_signal is untested (score 2); before committing to build, one outreach batch to the Craft CMS Slack/Discord to confirm purchase intent is warranted. Stage is validate rather than build because of zero responsiveness data.
solution_plan: The micro-service is a paid Craft CMS plugin (Formie add-on) that connects Formie form submissions to HubSpot's Communication Preferences API, enabling proper GDPR opt-in consent flows without manual workarounds. The factory builds it by writing the plugin code with Claude (Craft CMS plugin architecture is well-documented), setting up a Gumroad or Lemon Squeezy storefront ($149/site license), a one-page landing page explaining the GDPR compliance angle, and an automated license-key delivery email. To sell, the factory drafts targeted messages to the Craft CMS Discord (#plugins channel), the Craft CMS community forum, and GitHub watchers of the Formie plugin; outreach goes out only after Youval approves each batch. Once a customer pays, they get a download link and license key automatically; support questions go to a shared inbox Claude monitors; Stripe/Lemon Squeezy handles renewals. The only recurring human touch is Youval approving outreach batches and reviewing new support tickets flagged by Claude as needing operator judgment.
notes: All build_gates technically pass at the validate threshold, but responsiveness_signal = 2 means the market hasn't been probed. Run one outreach batch (30-50 targeted messages in Craft CMS community) and confirm 2+ purchase expressions before committing to build. Niche is small — size the TAM carefully before investing full build effort.
